integrity: The arbitrary-dimensional proof uses only standard convex facts: the normal cone on the relative interior equals the orthogonal complement of the affine-hull direction space; every relative-boundary point has a nonzero supporting normal inside that direction space; and relative interior is dense. The resulting Hausdorff jump is bounded below by the truncation radius. The packaged computation checks examples only and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only the direct truncated normal-cone map used as form (3) in the primary source, for nonempty closed convex sets and fixed positive truncation radius. It does not apply to the source's distinct multiplier-bounded manifold construction (4), does not address arbitrary nonconvex sets, and does not by itself provide an alternative convergence proof outside Assumption 2.
title: Affine-subspace rigidity of Hausdorff-Lipschitz truncated normal cones
